newsitem.title: CHINA: China expenditure grows less than revenue in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China expenditure grows less than revenue in 1996.

text.p: Chinese government expenditure grew more slowly than revenues in 1996 but Beijing is still struggling to narrow its budget deficit, Minister of Finance Liu Zhongli said on Sunday.

The gap between income and expenditure remained so large it would be difficult for China to achieve its target of eliminating the deficit by the year 2000, Liu told the National People's Congress, or parliament, in his annual budget speech.
Total revenues in 1996 came to 736.661 billion yuan ($88.754 billion), up 18 percent compared with 1995, while total expenditures were 791.438 billion yuan, up 16 percent, he said.
The 1996 budget deficit was 10.8 percent below the budgeted target, reaching 54.777 billion yuan, he said.
"On the whole, revenue for 1996 increased by a big margin, and the trend of the drop in the ratio of revenue to GDP (Gross Domestic Product) was reversed," he said.
Widespread tax evasion and difficulties reining in spending continued to hamper efforts to cut the deficit, he said.

"Huge debts are incurred in the central budget. Losses in taxation are still serious," he said. "Extravagance and waste are very prevalent...The tax base is being seriously eroded by extra-budgetary charges."
